`du`: estimate file space usage.

## Synopsis

<strong>du</strong> \[<strong>-asbhc</strong>\] \[<strong>-d</strong> <em>n</em>\] \[<em>path</em>...\]

## Description

<strong>du</strong> prints how much each directory under each <em>path</em> holds, everything inside it counted, deepest first and the <em>path</em> itself last. Each line is a size, a tab, and the path. With no <em>path</em>, it uses <strong>.</strong>.

Sizes are in 1 KiB blocks: each file takes its size rounded up to whole blocks. Symbolic links are counted as themselves and never followed (as GNU <strong>du</strong>'s <strong>-P</strong>). A file given as a <em>path</em> is always printed.

## Options

<strong>-a</strong>
: Print each file too, not only directories.

<strong>-s</strong>
: Print only a total for each <em>path</em> given (the same as <strong>-d 0</strong>).

<strong>-h</strong>
: Print sizes in human-readable form, in powers of 1024 (for example <strong>1.5K</strong>, <strong>2M</strong>).

<strong>-b</strong>
: Print sizes in bytes, the files' real sizes, not rounded to blocks. It takes precedence over <strong>-h</strong>.

<strong>-c</strong>
: Print a grand total of all the <em>path</em>s at the end, labeled <strong>total</strong>.

<strong>-d</strong> <em>n</em>, <strong>--max-depth</strong> <em>n</em>
: Print directories (and with <strong>-a</strong>, files) only down to <em>n</em> levels below each <em>path</em>; everything deeper is still counted.

Single-letter options may be combined, as in <strong>-sh</strong>.

## Exit status

0 on success; 1 if a path could not be read or an option was invalid.

## Examples

```text
du -sh /home
du -ad 1 /lib
du -sc /bin /lib
```

## Notes

The <strong>--max-depth=n</strong> form is not supported; give the number as the next argument.

## See also

<strong>df</strong>(1), <strong>ls</strong>(1), <strong>find</strong>(1), <strong>tree</strong>(1)
